transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-18
Start time: 15:30 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martin (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Catalyst PM), Jared Lopez (Catalyst Eng Lead), Samir Patel (Catalyst CTO)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping to align success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan and integration approach. Main focus: OpenAI-compatible endpoints, SDKs, function/tool calling, structured output and evaluation metrics. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send POC template and examples; Catalyst to provide workload samples and security questions.

Topics:
- Success criteria (latency, cost, accuracy)
- Workload sizing & traffic patterns
- Benchmarks + evaluation harness
- Integration: SDKs, openai-compatible API, tool/function calling, structured output (JSON schema)
- Security & compliance asks (SOC2, KMS, VPC)

Action items (recorded in notes): see metadata section.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining uh i'm alex from redwood inference, i'll kick us off. um priya from our SE team is here as well. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Maya (Catalyst): good thanks, yeah excited to dig in. couple people on our side - jared and samir with me.
[00:18] Jared (Catalyst): hey hi, morning.
[00:20] Priya (Redwood): hi all, quick agenda: align on success criteria, get your workload numbers, propose bench plan and talk integration steps (sdks + open a i compatible endpoints).
[00:34] Samir (Catalyst): perfect, we mainly want to validate cost/latency tradeoffs for our chat summarization pipeline and tool calling for downstream analytics.
[00:43] Alex (Redwood): great — can you give a bit more color on traffic? like qps, average tokens per session, retention?
[00:51] Maya (Catalyst): yeah so currently in prod we have about 5k active chat sessions per day, peak concurrency maybe 800-1k concurrent users during spikes. average session is about 2.2k tokens, but that includes system + history. weekly token volume ballpark is 10 million tokens. these are ballpark numbers.
[01:15] Jared (Catalyst): and our latency target is 1.5s p95 on short responses (<=150 tokens) and under 3.5s p95 for full summarization across 1k qps peak if possible. cost target is really important — we'd like to be competitive vs current vendor.
[01:34] Priya (Redwood): okay that's super helpful. for the POC we typically simulate a representative slice: synthetic sessions matching your token distribution and 1k r/s peak for 15 mins to stress. we'll show batch versus single request modes and also try prefix caching. note: our terms for dedicated vs hosted will change cost and latency.
[01:58] Maya (Catalyst): can you explain the hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs briefly? cause procurement leans toward hosted but sec wants private options.
[02:06] Alex (Redwood): hosted = fastest onboarding, pay-as-you-go; dedicated = reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower per-token unit cost; private = VPC/on-prem for compliance. you can start hosted for speed then migrate to dedicated or private.
[02:28] Samir (Catalyst): our security checklist: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, per-request audit logs, KMS integration, and data residency in eu-west - are those covered?
[02:39] Priya (Redwood): yes we support SOC2, SAML/SSO, audit logs and KMS/HSM integrations; for residency we have region support — we'll attach the security pack and SOC2 report.
[02:49] Alex (Redwood): i'll include the security links in the follow-up (redwood security pack url, poc template and pricing).
[02:55] Maya (Catalyst): appreciated. on integration — we use node and python clients and currently call Open A I compatible endpoints. we want to keep that surface so minimal effort for engineers.
[03:07] Priya (Redwood): good news: we provide OpenAI-compatible endpoints and language SDKs (Python/Node). we'll share sample snippets for tool calling and structured output; we also have an example for function/tool calling as a drop-in.
[03:20] Jared (Catalyst): when you say function calling, do you mean the Open A I style function call spec? we rely heavily on structured json outputs for downstream parsing.
[03:28] Priya (Redwood): yes — we support function/tool calling and structured output with schema enforcement. small caveat: for large schemas we recommend validating post-response; we'll demo a few strategies.
[03:42] Samir (Catalyst): what's the typical latency hit for tool-calling versus plain text generation?
[03:48] Priya (Redwood): depends — if you do multi-step tool invocation there's roundtrip, but for single response structured outputs overhead is minimal. we'll test both in benchmarks.
[03:59] Alex (Redwood): ok let's sketch success criteria — maybe we propose: p95 latency <=1.5s for short responses, accuracy/QA thresholds based on your eval set, and cost target within 20% of current spend. thoughts?
[04:13] Maya (Catalyst): that sounds reasonable. for accuracy we have an internal correctness dataset for summarization — we'll share sample prompts and labels.
[04:21] Jared (Catalyst): and we want determinism for structured outputs — e.g., for JSON output we need stable keys and limited hallucination.
[04:30] Priya (Redwood): we'll instrument a schema validator during the bench run and produce a hallucination rate metric.
[04:38] Alex (Redwood): great. on workload sizing — can you give us distribution of short vs long requests?
[04:44] Maya (Catalyst): approx 65% short (<=150 tokens), 25% mid (150-800 tokens), 10% long (>800 tokens). but the long ones drive KV cache/memory use.
[04:57] Priya (Redwood): good — we'll include models with kv cache behavior in the POC. also, are you amenable to quantized model variants for cost testing?
[05:07] Samir (Catalyst): yes but we need to confirm quality delta. we'll specify AB tests and guardrails.
[05:14] Alex (Redwood): timeline — propose two-week POC prep (we align on artifacts and baseline), one-week bench runs, then one-week analysis and scorecard; total ~4 weeks. does that work?
[05:25] Maya (Catalyst): procurement timeline is tight, but four weeks is ok. if we can parallelize sample data prep with security review that'd speed things.
[05:34] Jared (Catalyst): can you run benchmarks against both hosted and dedicated to show difference?
[05:39] Priya (Redwood): yes we can run hosted first, then mirror a dedicated config (we'll emulate reserved capacity) to show latency/cost delta. note that true dedicated numbers need reserved infra but we can approximate.
[05:52] Samir (Catalyst): what's the SDK drop-in like? we currently call open a i endpoints and use their tooling for function calling. how much change?
[06:00] Priya (Redwood): minimal. the open a i compatible endpoint means you usually only change the base url and api key; we provide sample wrappers. we'll also give a Node example for streaming responses and function calls.
[06:13] Jared (Catalyst): cool. about structured output: we need output to be checked against our schema and any missing fields to be flagged. will you provide schema validation hooks?
[06:22] Priya (Redwood): yes; we can include a post-processing validator in the bench harness; optionally we can run a constrained generation mode with templates to reduce hallucination.
[06:32] Alex (Redwood): quick note on metrics we'll produce in bench: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, hallucination rate vs schema, function-calling success rate.
[06:46] Maya (Catalyst): love that. also need memory/kv cache footprint numbers because our infra has limited GPU memory.
[06:53] Priya (Redwood): we'll capture GPU memory usage and model footprint. for quantized models we'll show perf vs memory tradeoffs.
[07:02] Alex (Redwood): questions from procurement/security?
[07:06] Samir (Catalyst): we need to review contractual SLAs and data residency specifics. also curious about audit logs retention and who can access them.
[07:16] Alex (Redwood): we have configurable retention, role-based access, and audit logs delivered to your SIEM via forwarders; i'll include details in the security packet.
[07:25] Maya (Catalyst): okay logistics — who will run the bench harness? redwood or catalyst?
[07:30] Priya (Redwood): we can run it and provide the harness so you can reproduce on your side. recommended: redwood runs initial bench with your sample data, then we'll hand over the harness.
[07:41] Jared (Catalyst): license/contract question — will you provide terms for a short-term dedicated reservation for the POC so numbers look realistic?
[07:50] Alex (Redwood): we can offer a short-term reserved capacity for bench runs in the POC under a demo agreement; we'll surface pricing in the follow-up.
[07:59] Maya (Catalyst): great. any blockers on integration?
[08:03] Priya (Redwood): only if your infra needs special network peering for private deployment; otherwise open a i compatible hosted path is basically plug-and-play.
[08:12] Samir (Catalyst): we do have VPC peering requests for private later, we'll send network contact details.
[08:18] Alex (Redwood): noted. i'll include contact and next steps.
[08:22] Maya (Catalyst): also, do you support streaming summarization callbacks? we use streaming to progressively show results to users.
[08:30] Priya (Redwood): yes we support streaming responses and will demo it. for streaming + function calling we have examples. small note: streaming p95 tends to be influenced by batch sizes.
[08:44] Jared (Catalyst): for the bench, can we include a mix of streaming and non-streaming sessions?
[08:49] Priya (Redwood): yes we'll configure the harness accordingly.
[08:53] Alex (Redwood): let's capture concrete success criteria for the POC doc: 1) latency: p95 <=1.5s for short, <=3.5s for long 2) hallucination/schema error rate <3% 3) cost per 1M tokens within 20% of your current vendor 4) streaming behavior acceptable (no more than 10% degraded sessions).
[09:18] Maya (Catalyst): ok good to record that.
[09:20] Samir (Catalyst): what models will you test? open question.
[09:24] Priya (Redwood): we'll test a curated set: small/fast model (low latency), a mid-size baseline, and a quantized variant; and if helpful we can add your preferred model. we'll also run an eval on your labeled dataset.
[09:38] Jared (Catalyst): for the POC harness, what inputs do you need from us?
[09:42] Priya (Redwood): sample prompts + label set for accuracy, token distribution, expected qps, and network constraints (eg ip allowlists). also service account keys for test env if you want us to run with your samples behind a VPC.
[09:58] Maya (Catalyst): we'll prepare a sample set of 2k sessions and the labeled summarization set.
[10:04] Alex (Redwood): perfect. artifacts we'll share: POC template, security pack (SOC2), SDK snippets (python/node), bench harness link and a short recording of the tool-calling demo. links will be in follow-up.
[10:16] Maya (Catalyst): any competitors or gotchas we should be aware of? our procurement comparing to open a i and anthro (anthropic) for safety.
[10:25] Alex (Redwood): noted; we'll include a comparison sheet. some transcription note: apologies if i mis-said anthopic earlier, it was anthropic.
[10:33] Priya (Redwood): also for quantization — sometimes quantized variants show small accuracy drop; we'll present results so you can decide.
[10:41] Samir (Catalyst): budget-wise we have a cap for the POC; please include an estimate for the hosted bench and estimated dedicated pricing.
[10:49] Alex (Redwood): will do.
[10:51] Maya (Catalyst): ok timeline recap?
[10:53] Alex (Redwood): proposed: prep (2 weeks) — you send samples & security asks; redwood prepares bench, configs. bench runs (1 week) — redwood runs hosted + approx dedicated. analysis (1 week) — result scorecard and recommended config. total ~4 weeks.
[11:06] Jared (Catalyst): works for us. we'll try to get the samples to you by friday (2025-11-22).
[11:12] Priya (Redwood): i'll set up a benchmark kickoff meeting once we have the samples; also will attach SDK snippets in the follow-up so eng can start low-effort testing.
[11:21] Alex (Redwood): ok final recap / next steps: (1) Alex to send POC doc, pricing and security pack (2) Priya to share SDK examples + bench harness + demo recording (3) Catalyst to share sample data, qps numbers, network constraints by 2025-11-22 (4) schedule bench kickoff next week.
[11:36] Maya (Catalyst): thanks all. excited to see the numbers.
[11:40] Samir (Catalyst): great, thanks.
[11:42] Alex (Redwood): thanks everyone talk soon.
